logline: Two kernels heat in one pan; the sealed one bursts into a flake and jumps, the one with a hairline crack leaks its steam and ends up at the bottom of the bowl.
ending: The flake drops into the bowl, the camera sinks to the bottom, and the dry cracked kernel lies there among the unpopped: their steam got out.
opening_promise: A cross-section of a popcorn bowl reveals two hard kernels at the bottom, with the question of why they never popped.

continuity.what: Two kernels, one sealed and one cracked, from the pan to the bowl; the cracked one is the kernel the opening asked about.

style_sheet.look: Risograph science zine: off-white paper, overprinted flat inks (blue linework, fluorescent pink, yellow) with 3-unit misregistration, halftone dot shading, paper grain; cutaway diagrams instead of characters.
style_sheet.materials: ink on paper: multiply-blended fills, halftone dots for shade, blue line outlines printed slightly off register
style_sheet.environment: a cross-section bowl and a skillet over riso flames; a print-style thermometer gauge fixed at the top of the frame during the pan scenes is the only measurement on screen
style_sheet.framing: vertical: pan in the lower third, open space above for steam and the jump; the camera pushes into whichever kernel the line is about and follows the jump up
style_sheet.typography: Inter 900 (OFL) for three readouts only: WATER 14%, 180 °C on the top gauge, and REPLAY
style_sheet.sound_intent: A clear, warm narrator (approved voice af_heart at natural speed) over a curious pluck score; the score holds its breath before the burst; crack, hiss, pop and foam are sound-designed and the replay places the pop on the steam jet, not the crack.

audio.music: original note-list score synthesised in code
audio.sfx: seeded procedural sound design on the moment table

shots.sees: a cross-section bowl of popcorn; the camera sinks to two hard kernels at the bottom
two kernels in a cold pan open like a diagram: soft starch, blue water drops, a hard shiny hull that glints
shots.after: kernels in cutaway with water visible

shots.sees: the flame lights, the thermometer passes 100 °C, water drops boil into bubbles; in the sealed kernel bubbles crowd and the hull bulges and trembles
the camera finds a hairline crack in the right kernel; steam hisses out of it in a plume, its bubbles drain away and its hull relaxes and browns
the thermometer reaches 180 °C; the sealed hull splits, petals of hull fold back and white starch foam blooms out in slow motion; a leg of starch presses the pan and the kernel jumps
shots.after: a popcorn flake in the air

shots.sees: a replay of the burst: the hull cracks silently, then the steam jet bursts out and sound rings spread from the jet
shots.after: the pop tied to the steam

shots.sees: the flake drops into the bowl and the camera sinks to the bottom where the dry cracked kernel lies

hardest_shot.why: The burst must look like real popcorn forming (hull splitting, foam lobes blooming into a recognisable flake) and the leg-kick jump must read as a physical push on the pan; a generic white blob or a cut would lose the payoff.
hardest_shot.fallback: Stage the burst as a cut from a straining kernel to a fully formed flake mid-air with a sound accent, and drop the leg line.

claims.statement: A popcorn kernel's hard hull (the pericarp) acts as a pressure vessel while it heats.
claims.source_title: Hoseney, Zeleznak & Abdelrahman (1983), Mechanism of popcorn popping, Journal of Cereal Science 1(1): 43-52 (catalogue record and abstract)
claims.excerpt: the pericarp acts as a pressure vessel during popping
claims.spoken_as: sealed in a hard, shiny hull / In a sealed kernel it's trapped, and the pressure climbs.
claims.note: Excerpt relayed through a web-search summary of the abstract; the catalogue and publisher pages were not reachable from this session (network policy).

claims.statement: Heated, part of the kernel's water turns to vapour; trapped by the hull, it raises the pressure inside.
claims.source_title: Virot & Ponomarenko (2015) abstract; Hoseney, Zeleznak & Abdelrahman (1983) abstract
claims.excerpt: the critical temperature 180°C at which almost all of popcorn pops is consistent with an elementary pressure vessel scenario (Virot & Ponomarenko); the pericarp acts as a pressure vessel during popping (Hoseney et al.)
claims.spoken_as: Heat turns some of that water to steam.
claims.note: Inference from the pressure-vessel model both sources describe; the narration says "some of that water" because most of it stays liquid (superheated) until the hull breaks.

claims.statement: Popcorn kernels hold roughly 13 to 14.5 percent water by weight.
claims.source_title: Purdue University College of Agriculture news (2020), quoting food scientist Bruce Hamaker
claims.excerpt: Popcorn must have moisture inside the kernel of about 13 to 14.5 percent of its total weight
claims.spoken_as: a little water, about fourteen percent
claims.note: Expert quotation in a university news article (secondary); excerpt relayed through web search.

claims.statement: Kernels with cracks or weak spots in the hull let moisture escape while heating, and fail to pop.
claims.source_title: Purdue University College of Agriculture news (2020)
claims.excerpt: 4 to 47 percent of kernels, dependent on variety, were unsuccessful in their transformation ... cracks or weak spots in the outer layer that let moisture escape during heating
claims.spoken_as: a kernel with one tiny crack just leaks its steam away / Their steam got out.
claims.note: Excerpt relayed through web search. The film generalises from cracks and weak spots to one visible crack; that simplification is listed under dramatization.

claims.statement: Almost all popcorn pops at a critical temperature of about 180 degrees Celsius.
claims.source_title: Virot & Ponomarenko (2015), Popcorn: critical temperature, jump and sound, J. R. Soc. Interface 12: 20141247 (abstract)
claims.excerpt: the critical temperature 180°C at which almost all of popcorn pops is consistent with an elementary pressure vessel scenario
claims.spoken_as: At about a hundred and eighty degrees, the hull bursts
claims.note: Abstract text relayed through web search of the HAL archive record; publisher host not reachable from this session.

claims.statement: Superheated water provides the driving force that expands the kernel once the hull ruptures.
claims.source_title: Hoseney, Zeleznak & Abdelrahman (1983), Mechanism of popcorn popping (abstract)
claims.excerpt: most of the water in the kernel is superheated at the moment of popping and provides the driving force for expanding the kernel once the pericarp ruptures
claims.spoken_as: and the hot starch puffs into foam
claims.note: Excerpt relayed through a web-search summary of the abstract. 'Foam' is the film's plain word for the expanded starch.

claims.statement: Popcorn jumps on a leg of starch that is compressed against the surface.
claims.excerpt: We observe that popcorn jumps with a 'leg' of starch which is compressed on the ground.
claims.spoken_as: A leg of starch kicks the pan, and the kernel jumps.

claims.statement: The researchers propose that the familiar pop sound is caused by the release of water vapour.
claims.excerpt: By synchronizing video recordings with acoustic recordings, we propose that the familiar 'pop' sound of the popcorn is caused by the release of water vapour.
claims.spoken_as: And the pop? Researchers think it's the steam rushing out.
claims.note: The authors propose this; the narration says 'think' rather than stating it as settled.

dramatization: Kernels are drawn several hundred times life size in cutaway; real kernels are opaque.
Water is drawn as a few visible drops and steam as bubbles; in reality the water is spread through the starch.
The burst and jump are slowed down by orders of magnitude, and the replay separates the crack from the steam jet more than real time would.
Unpopped kernels fail for several reasons (cracks, weak spots, moisture loss); the film shows a single visible crack.
Steam is drawn as white bubbles that merge as the pressure rises; in a real kernel most of the water stays liquid (superheated) under pressure until the hull breaks, then flashes to vapour.
